messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert INC-8471 triggered: spike in 5xx (500/502/504) from /v1/generate in us-west1. Estimated error rate 6.8% over last 5m. Paging oncall-maya :rotating_light:
oncall-maya: acked. jumping in now. pulling top-level dashboards and traces.
oncall-maya: quick look: per-model 5xx shows model: redwood/13b-quant has biggest spike. latency also up.
oncall-maya: checking runtime logs for segfaults / oom entries. running: `gcloud logging read "resource.type=global severity>=ERROR" --limit 50 --project=redwood-platform`
eng-runtime-joe: im on it. seeing repeated kernel OOMs on runner-hosts handling long-context batched requests. attaching recent stderr from runner (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-15T20:03:12Z] model-runner[pid=4123]: kv-cache alloc failed: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-15T20:03:12Z] model-runner[pid=4123]: segfault (signal 11) at 0x7ff... stack trace ... llama_kernel_execute+0x1a3
[2026-03-15T20:03:13Z] supervisor: process 4123 exited with code 139
```
eng-runtime-joe: looks like large-batch requests with long seq-length are exhausting GPU memory on the quantized kernels; on some hosts the process is crashing (sig11) which cascades to 502s at the gateway.
eng-sre-liam: are we seeing host-level OOM (oom-killer) or cuda OOM?
eng-runtime-joe: mostly cuda OOM and then segfault during cleanup. not seeing kernel panics at hypervisor level.
oncall-maya: immediate mitigation: 1) throttle /v1/generate for affected customer routes by 50% 2) enable model fallback to smaller model variant 3) drain warm pool hosts running quantized variant and move traffic to gpus with larger memory. can someone run those?
eng-sre-liam: I can apply the throttle at the gateway. doing a quick NGINX rate-limit patch via console.
eng-sre-liam: patch applied: rate-limit 60r/m per token for routes tagged customer=high-traffic. monitoring.
product-ana: FYI this might impact prod traffic for two large customers (acct-redwood-a, acct-beta). please coordinate with CS before longer mitigation.
customer-success-jess: got it. i'll message both accounts with a short heads-up (no details) once we confirm mitigation is working.
eng-runtime-joe: second mitigation: enable automatic fallback in routing policy to `redwood/13b-quant-safe` (lower batch memory profile) and reduce max-batch-size from 64 to 16 for the affected pool. applying now.
eng-runtime-joe: CLI to update route (run by runtime ops):
```bash
redwoodctl routes update --route /v1/generate --region us-west1 --fallback-model redwood/13b-quant-safe --max-batch-size 16
```
eng-runtime-joe: applied. initiating graceful drain of 4 hosts in pool quant-gpu-pool-3.
oncall-maya: rolling logs look better, 5xx dropped from 6.8% -> 2.1% in the first 90s after throttling+fallback. still seeing a handful of crash loops on old hosts.
eng-sre-liam: i'll cordon and reprovision those 3 crashy hosts. suspects: recent driver update from last night (nvidia 532.41) + quant kernel edge-case. rolling them back to 530.x while we investigate.
eng-runtime-joe: for debugging: capturing core dumps and enabling debug symbols on a non-prod replicate. pushed debug image to test cluster. will run synthetic load with long-context requests to reproduce.
eng-runtime-joe: preliminary root cause hypothesis: quantized kernel has a memory accounting bug when prefix cache + long context + large batch coincide, leading to invalid free on cleanup -> segfault.
product-ana: potential customer impact: error rates affected ~2% of total generate requests in us-west1 over last 15m. customers with heavy long-context chat flows saw higher failure rates (~8-12% per-account).
customer-success-jess: drafting outbound: "We're investigating intermittent 5xx errors affecting LLM generations in us-west1. We've applied temporary throttles and fallback routing; service is recovering. We'll follow up with details." want approvals?
product-ana: fine to send now. tag eng-runtime in case CS gets deep follow-ups.
eng-sre-liam: rolling host replacements done. crashy hosts out of service. observing memory usage per GPU trending down.
oncall-maya: monitoring metrics: 5xx now 0.6% and trending. latency went up slightly for fallback model (~120ms p95 delta).
eng-runtime-joe: next steps: 1) add guard in quant kernel to check allocation deltas 2) increase telemetry on kv-cache alloc/frees to catch mismatch 3) revert driver on prod hosts until kernel fix validated 4) run canary with worst-case synthetic workload
eng-runtime-joe: tagging follow-up ticket: INF-2026 with reproducer and debug logs.
customer-success-jess: update sent to customers at 20:28 PT. no escalation yet.
eng-sre-liam: lowering priority of page to standby. keep monitoring for 30m.
oncall-maya: thanks all. oncall ends shift notes: incident type: runtime OOM -> segfault -> 5xx cascade. mitigations applied: throttles, fallback routing, host rollback/drain. impact: partial request failures for long-context heavy customers in us-west1 ~2% of total. follow-ups assigned to eng-runtime for kernel fix and infra for driver validation. :white_check_mark:
